key_insight: SAO makes asynchronous RL for agentic LLMs more stable and effective by switching from group-wise to single-rollout sampling and adding strict token-level clipping.
engineering_relevance: The method is practical for large-scale agentic training pipelines because it improves throughput-friendly asynchronous optimization without sacrificing training stability.
method: Use one rollout per prompt instead of group-wise sampling to reduce off-policy drift.
Train value models with practical designs tailored to single-rollout asynchronous updates.
Apply strict double-side token-level clipping to stabilize optimization over long runs.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports stable training for 1,000 steps and consistent gains over GRPO variants on SWE-Bench Verified, BeyondAIME, and IMOAnswerBench, plus success in simulated online learning.
watch_item: Single-rollout asynchronous training may require careful value-model and clipping configuration to avoid instability or under-updating in more complex deployments.
paper_title: Single-Rollout Asynchronous Optimization for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
